description: We are a team of highschool it teachers passionate about technology, education and new ways to think about problems. We came to event as tutors but decide to also join as a team.
summary: AtuelSAR aims to address the lack of accessible tools for transforming ground-based SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite data into useful information for identifying potential deformation anomalies and displacements on mountain slopes. In areas such as Valle Grande—located in San Rafael, Mendoza, Argentina—where landslides can compromise roads, infrastructure, and public safety, the platform enables the monitoring of terrain changes, the visualization of areas exhibiting unusual behavior, and the establishment of priorities for preventive inspections by the relevant authorities. In this way, it contributes to more informed geological risk management, facilitating decision-making without replacing technical on-site assessments.
details: During the hackathon, we developed a functional prototype of AtuelSAR, consisting of a satellite data processing system and a digital visualization platform. The tool utilizes NISAR radar observations and interferometry (InSAR) techniques to compare images from different dates, establish a historical baseline of the terrain, and identify potential deformation anomalies. This analysis is complemented by topographic information from NASADEM and meteorological data from NASA POWER. The results are presented through georeferenced maps, temporal evolution charts, and indicators that classify areas into three levels—Normal, Attention, and Alert—based on the model’s criteria. In this way, we created a tool accessible via computers and mobile devices that transforms complex satellite data into understandable information, helping to guide preventive inspections and support decision-making.
